CLSA on Chola Invest

O-P, TP Rs 1970

3% PAT beat vs estimates in 1QFY27, driven by a 5% PPOP beat, partly offset by higher-than-expected credit costs.

Overall, it was a good quarter.

Disbursement and AUM growth both were in the low-20s while NIM was largely stable on a sequential basis.

Stronger-than-expected fees and lower-than-expected opex helped drive the beat on PPOP.

Asset quality improved with the calculated net slippage ratio declining 40bps YoY to 2.5% driven by an improvement in vehicle finance and CSEL; there is room for further reduction as it is still above 1QFY25 levels.

Management sounded confident on the analyst call.

Macquarie on Chola Invest

U-P, TP Rs 1495

Delivered a strong 1Q FY27, with PAT rising 46% YoY to Rs16.5bn, broadly in line with estimates.

Better cost-to-income of 36% (vs 40% MQe) offset softer-than-expected 8.2% NIM (vs 8.5% MQe).

Credit cost was broadly in line, while AUM grew 22% YoY, led by LAP, SBPL, and SME.

RoA expanded 50bps YoY to 2.8%.

Despite decent performance, valuation remains stretched at a 3.4x FY28E P/BV, assuming 2.7% ROA

Jefferies on HUL

Buy, TP Rs 2850

While HUL's 1Q was a slight miss, 7% share price drop is baffling given extent of miss.

There were a few weak spots (Home Care margins; growth in Personal Care & Foods), but offsetting factors meant the overall miss in EBITDA was small.

Also note consistent improvement in growth & profitability over past few qtrs.

Mgmt. commentary was reasonable, with expectations of stable demand & margin remaining in the guided range.

JPM on Varun Beverages

Neutral, TP Rs 530

Management tried to address key investor concerns, though a few pressure points remain visible.

Even as domestic volume growth is trending 20%+ in most months, weather-related disruptions can still weigh on reported growth, as witnessed in Q2 (April flat).

Management sounded confident of sustaining healthy double-digit growth, though delivery is increasingly reliant on sharper Rs20 propositions and scale-up of adjacencies

Competitive intensity remains elevated, particularly at lower price points (aiding category expansion), and VBL is prioritizing profitable growth over aggressively chasing low-margin Rs10 volumes.

International territories continue to fare well, led by broad-based Africa momentum, though Twizza integration/scale-up and Kenya expansion (post acquisition) will be key watch points.

VBL trades at 39x/34x CY27/28E P/E
Although see limited downside at current levels, domestic volume growth delivery (1HCY26 2 yr CAGR +~8%) will be a key share price catalyst.

CITI on Varun Beverages

Buy, TP cut to Rs 580 from Rs 640

India volumes grew 14% (off a -7% base) primarily impacted by weather-led disruption in April.

Key investor debate at VBL remains whether growth trajectory has structurally moderated amid increased competitive intensity in India; note that despite competitive pressures, India volumes delivered an 8% CAGR over past two years in 1HCY26.

Going ahead, while mgmt. commentary remains constructive, calling out sustained 20%+ volume growth trends extending into July, note that 2H accounts for only 35% of annual volumes. 

Believe category remains attractive (penetration-led growth opportunity) over long-term & competitive intensity could be gradually easing with Campa reducing volumes in its Rs10 SKU – we would look for an acceleration in 2-year CAGR trajectory.

GS on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 4370

L&T's P&M (core) order inflow was 17% yoy in 1QFY27 (vs. GSe of -6%), and 1Q core EBITDA margins came in at 6.9% (vs. GSe of 7.1%) a 20bps decline yoy, driven by lower execution in core segments.

Key highlights from quarter:

1) Prospect base being resilient at Rs15tn despite strong order inflow in Q1 and well spread across domestic as well as international with private sector representing 45% in the mix.

2) Project execution continued to be impacted amid West Asia conflict, reflected in weaker execution;

3) FY27 guidance maintained at +10-12% on order inflows and similar growth in revenue with core margins flat (7.8% excluding realty biz. and 8.2% including realty).

Mgt highlighted that award and tendering in ME continues.

Jefferies on L&T

Buy, TP Rs 5000

Q1 EBITDA was 8% lower than expectations as E&C execution was weak.

14% YoY rise in order flow is tracking L&T’s annual 10-12% YoY growth guidance.

Management maintained its annual 10-12% YoY revenue guidance, implying that 2H will be better, but likely conditional on war settling down

Believe L&T stock should see a leg up to Rs4278 (when conflict started) if global tensions ease, with earnings visibility adding to upside thereon.

CITI on Supreme Ind

Sell, TP Rs 3150

1Q EBITDA was up 25% yoy despite 14% lower volumes (channel destocking) on higher EBITDA margins (14.6% vs 12.2% in 1QFY26).

EBITDA margin improvement was likely driven by a combination of lower cost PVC inventory, better product mix, and inventory loss recorded in 1QFY26.

Plastic piping segment volumes were down ~15% yoy, EBIT/kg was Rs16.3/kg vs 19.9/kg in 4Q and Rs10.6/kg in 1QFY26.

Looking ahead, mgmt. has reiterated their guidance for 15-17% volume growth in the plastic piping segment (12-13% overall).

This implies a 26% yoy volume growth in piping segment for balance 9MFY27.

Considering modest growth indicated by mgmt. for May/Jun (in a relatively stable PVC price environment), think there could be downside risk to the FY27 volume guidance.

CLSA on Supreme Ind

Hold, TP Rs 4000

Q1 in-line , as weak sales volumes (-14% YoY) were partly offset by higher margins (on a better mix).

Management maintained its FY27 guidance of 12%-13% volume growth & a 14%-14.5% Ebitda margin

This looks demanding, despite recovering PVC prices, given ask rate for the rest of year is 20%+ on a high base.

CITI on SAIL 

Sell, TP Rs 160 

1Q EBITDA rose 72% yoy largely on higher realizations (+13%); volumes fell 9%, costs rose 4%. 

Adj EBITDA/t: Rs10,715 vs. Rs8,280 in 4Q; Rs5,695 last year. 

QoQ EBITDA/t move – higher realizations (Rs5,870/t), offset by higher costs (~Rs3,430). 

Call highlights: 

1) 1Q volumes fell ~9% yoy -planned shutdowns, SAIL is maintaining FY27 volume target at ~13%. 

2) July flats prices at Rs56,900 vs. Rs57,200 in 1Q; longs at Rs54,200 vs. Rs57,100. 

3) Coking coal higher qoq in 1Q, SAIL expects a reduction in Aug/Sep. 

4) 1Q wage costs rose on VRS, wage revision due in Jan27. 

5) SAIL is targeting cost savings by FY29. 6) Net debt Rs217bn, FY27/28 capex Rs150bn/Rs200bn

 Sell: (1) Likely downside to EBITDA/t – domestic weakness + limited China upside, 

(2) Limited growth potential, next leg of capacities after 3 years, 

(3) Estimate net D/EBITDA at 2.5x+ by FY28.

UBS on Sail 

SELL, TP Rs 170 

(1) SAIL management highlighted that flat/long steel prices have corrected only Rs300/2,900 per ton in July as compared to Q1FY26 levels

(2) SAIL plans to increase its iron ore sales from 3.8mt in FY26 to 8.0mt in FY27, which is contingent on addressing logistical challenges. Q1FY27

iron ore sales at 1.1mt contributed to incremental sales/ profit of Rs4.0/1.5bn. 

(3) Over medium to long term, SAIL’s coking coal costs could materially decline as company aims to replace part of its imports.
 
SAIL plans to ramp up volumes from its Tasra captive mine, scheduled to commence operation from December 2026. 

(4) Management guided for capex to increase from Rs150bn in FY27 to above Rs200bn in FY28 and Rs250-260bn in FY29, primarily towards the expansion project at Burnpur
(IISCO plant).

Unified Data-Tech Solutions Ltd (Udtechs)

What the company does, in plain terms:
Udtechs is a system integrator. When a large business needs a data centre, cloud setup, networking or cybersecurity, a system integrator brings all the pieces together and makes them work as one. Think of it as the company that builds and connects the "engine rooms" of the digital world for other businesses.

The numbers, decoded:

Revenue for Q1 FY27 came in at around ₹106.23 crore, up from around ₹85.59 crore in the same quarter last year. That is a year-on-year growth of around 24.11%. In simple words, the company earned around a quarter more this time than it did in the same quarter a year ago.

The executable order book stood at around ₹100 crore plus as of July-end. An order book is work already won but not yet delivered. It gives some visibility on revenue that is already in hand.

Six new enterprise customers were added and billed during the quarter, including names such as Sun Pharma, Parle Agro and Apsara Plastic.
Winning recognisable customers is a sign the business is being trusted
with real work.

Two new OEM partners were added, Barracuda and Lightstorm. This widens
the range of products the company can offer and sell.

Why a novice should care:
Growing revenue while adding marquee customers and expanding the partner network is a healthy combination. The order book offers some comfort that this is not just a one quarter story.

The honest other side:
An order book of around ₹100 crore plus is close to a single quarter of revenue, so it is decent but not a multi-year cushion on its own. A business update is management's own framing. It highlights revenue and customer wins, but does not show margins, profit or cash flow. One strong top line quarter does not confirm the full year picture. System integration can also be a project lumpy, lower margin business, so the quality of profit matters as much as the growth number.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: RETAIL FUEL NETWORK OUTLOOK ⛽📍

• ⛽ Despite intense competition in the retail fuel market, TruAlt remains committed to its long-term downstream integration strategy, with expansion being carried out in a disciplined manner.

• 🏪 The company currently operates 7 retail fuel outlets, while 4 additional outlets are under construction.

• 📍 TruAlt has identified 76 additional high-potential locations across logistics corridors, highways, and rural-industrial regions for its phased retail network expansion.

• 📈 Future expansion will focus on sustainable operating economics, disciplined capital allocation, and strengthening the company's downstream fuel distribution network.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: SUSTAINABLE AVIATION FUEL (SAF) OUTLOOK ✈️🌱

• ✈️ Rising geopolitical tensions, aviation fuel price volatility, and global decarbonisation efforts are accelerating long-term demand for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).

• 🏭 TruAlt's proposed 100 million litres per annum Ethanol-to-Jet (ETJ/ATJ) SAF project positions the company in a high-margin, structurally undersupplied global market.

• 🌍 The Alcohol-to-Jet (ATJ) technology is a globally validated pathway for converting ethanol into SAF and allows blending of up to 50% with conventional Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) without major infrastructure changes.

• 📈 Global Net Zero commitments, CORSIA regulations, and emerging SAF blending mandates are expected to provide strong long-term demand visibility for low-carbon aviation fuels.

• 🤝 The company's MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board (APEDB) supports project development through infrastructure, land, and policy facilitation.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: CBG OUTLOOK 🌱♻️

• 🌍 Rising geopolitical tensions, global gas market disruptions, and the focus on India's energy security continue to strengthen the long-term outlook for the Compressed Biogas (CBG) industry.

• 🏛️ Continued policy support, including excise duty exemption on the biogas/CBG component in blended CNG, is expected to improve project economics and enhance long-term demand.

• 🤝 Strategic partnerships with Sumitomo Corporation and GAIL (India) Ltd. provide TruAlt with a scalable, institutionally backed platform for CBG expansion.

• 🏗️ Construction of CBG plants is progressing, with phased commissioning expected from FY27 onwards, while integrated feedstock sourcing and decentralized biomass ecosystems are expected to improve operational stability.

• 🚀 Management expects the CBG business to emerge as a significant long-term growth and earnings driver, aligned with India's clean energy transition and energy diversification goals.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: ETHANOL ; OUTLOOK REMAINS STRONG 🚀🌱

• ⛽ Management expects India's biofuel push to accelerate further, supported by E20 rollout, E22–E30 BIS standards, flex-fuel vehicles, and higher ethanol blending initiatives, improving long-term demand visibility.

• 🏭 The company's 1,300 KLPD dual-feed integration within its 2,000 KLPD installed capacity is expected to drive a near year-round, structurally resilient operating model.

• ⚙️ Focus remains on improving plant uptime, enhancing fermentation efficiency, and increasing capacity utilisation following operational stabilisation.

• ♻️ Co-products such as DDGS, CO₂ and other by-products are expected to increase non-fuel revenues, improve asset productivity, and support EBITDA margin expansion.

• 🚀 Management expects ethanol to remain the core cash flow engine, providing a strong foundation for expansion into emerging bioenergy businesses and positioning TruAlt to benefit from India's long-term energy transition.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: CBG EXPANSION ON TRACK WITH SUMITOMO & GAIL 🌱♻️

• 🏗️ Construction of 4 Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants under TruAlt Gas Pvt. Ltd. with Sumitomo Corporation is progressing as planned.

• 🤝 Through its JV with GAIL (India) Ltd., preparatory work for 6 additional CBG plants is advancing, with phased construction set to begin in the coming months.

• 🌍 Management sees CBG as one of India's fastest-growing renewable energy segments, backed by strong policy support.

• ♻️ The CBG business is expected to strengthen energy security, reduce import dependence, promote the circular economy and create rural economic value.

• 🚀 TruAlt expects the CBG segment to become a significant long-term growth driver for the company.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: ETHANOL ; DUAL-FEED PLATFORM DRIVES NEW GROWTH PHASE 🚀⛽

• 📈 Q1 FY27 marks the company's first year-on-year Q1 performance as a listed entity, with management highlighting strong execution.

• 🏭 Successfully integrated 1,300 KLPD of dual-feed capacity within its total 2,000 KLPD ethanol capacity, transforming into a near year-round producer.

• 🌾➡️⛽ Transition from a seasonal sugarcane-based model to a multi-feedstock ethanol platform improves operational flexibility and earnings potential.

• 🇮🇳 TruAlt now operates one of India's largest dual-feed ethanol platforms, capable of producing 5.5–6 crore litres of ethanol per month.

• 🎯 Management will focus on higher asset utilisation, operational efficiency, sustainable profitable growth and downstream value-added opportunities.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: MANAGEMENT REMAINS CONFIDENT ON ETHANOL GROWTH 🌾⛽

• 🇮🇳 Management said India's 20% ethanol blending target has been achieved five years ahead of schedule, reinforcing long-term demand for ethanol.

• 📈 Ethanol production capacity is nearing 2,000 crore litres per annum, making biofuels a key pillar of India's energy security and reducing crude oil imports.

• 🏛️ Despite temporary disruptions and lower allocations in ESY 2025–26, the company believes the industry's long-term structural outlook remains strong.

• 🤝 Expects continued policy stability and industry collaboration to support sustained growth of India's biofuel ecosystem.

• 🌍 Management highlighted that ethanol is a proven global fuel, with decades of successful adoption in countries like Brazil and the US, and stressed the need for fact-based public discourse.

TRUALT BIOENERGY Q1: GRAIN INTEGRATION BOOSTS CAPACITY & MARGINS 🌾⛽

• 🚀 Q1 FY27 marked the first full quarter after completing the grain integration programme, creating a new operational benchmark.

• 🏭 Installed ethanol capacity increased 43% YoY from 1,400 KLPD to 2,000 KLPD, with 65% capacity now dual-feed.

• 🌾 Diversified feedstock (grains + sugar derivatives) enables near year-round ethanol production, improves flexibility and lowers feedstock costs.

• 📈 Grain-based operations deliver ~6% higher profitability than sugar-based operations, supporting EBITDA and PBT margin expansion.

• ⚡ Current capacity utilisation stands at 60.57%, providing significant room for growth without major additional capex.

PREMIUM PLAST: ACQUIRES UNDER-CONSTRUCTION PLANT IN MP 🏭

• 🏗️ Acquired an under-construction manufacturing plant on a leasehold plot at MPIDC, Bagroda Industrial Area, Bhopal.

• 💰 Acquisition completed for ₹99 lakh (excluding stamp duty and registration charges).

• 📐 The facility spans 3,107.81 sq. ft. and has been acquired from Sky Heights Warehousing.

• 📈 The acquisition is aimed at expanding the company's business operations and manufacturing capacity.

• ✅ The transaction is not a related-party transaction, and the seller is unrelated to the promoters or management.

🟢 Impact: Positive (The acquisition supports capacity expansion and strengthens Premium Plast's manufacturing footprint.)

SEEMAX RESOURCES: COMPOUNDING APPLICATION REJECTED BY REGIONAL DIRECTOR ⚖️

• 📄 Regional Director (North Western Region) has rejected the company's compounding application filed under Section 441 of the Companies Act, 2013.

• ⚠️ The application pertained to an alleged violation of Section 185(1) of the Companies Act, 2013.

• 📅 The rejection order is dated July 14, 2026, and has now been received by the company.

• 👨‍⚖️ Seemax Resources is evaluating the order and may file an appeal or a fresh application, based on legal advice.

• 🏢 The company stated that there is no material impact on its operations as of now.

🔴 Impact: Negative (Regulatory setback due to rejection of the compounding application, though the company says there is currently no material operational impact.)

TANLA PLATFORMS: APPROVES ACQUISITION OF VALUEFIRST MIDDLE EAST FZC 🌍📲

• 🤝 Board approved acquisition of 100% stake in ValueFirst Middle East FZC (VF FZC) through subsidiary Karix Mobile FZ LLC.

• 🌍 VF FZC provides CPaaS (Communications Platform-as-a-Service) solutions and has operations across UAE, Saudi Arabia and Indonesia.

• 💰 Total enterprise value of the deal is AED 58.25 million (~₹148.52 crore), including ₹12 crore cash payment and assumption/discharge of liabilities.

• 📈 Acquisition will strengthen Tanla's presence in the Middle East, expand its enterprise customer base and improve administrative efficiencies.

• 📅 Transaction is expected to be completed by Q2 FY27, subject to agreed terms and conditions.

🟢 Impact: Positive (The acquisition expands Tanla's international CPaaS footprint, strengthens regional presence and supports long-term enterprise growth.)

TRUALT BIOENERGY: APPOINTS NEW CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD 👨‍💼

• 🏛️ Board has appointed Mr. Mallikarjun Bhimappa Dyaberi as Chairman of the Board for a one-year term, effective July 28, 2026.

• ✅ Mr. Dyaberi is already serving as an Independent Director of TruAlt Bioenergy.

• 🎓 Former IAS officer, with prior leadership roles including CEO of Tumkur Zilla Panchayat, Commissioner of Karnataka Housing Board, and Secretary to the Government of Karnataka (Labour Department).

• 🌱 Brings extensive experience in public administration, governance, policy-making and institutional leadership, expected to strengthen the company's strategic oversight.

🟢 Impact: Positive (The appointment adds experienced leadership and governance expertise to the Board, strengthening strategic decision-making.)

SIRCA PAINTS Q1: FY27 STRATEGIC PRIORITIES & OUTLOOK 🎯🎨

• 🏭 The company will scale the Wembley brand across India, accelerate manufacturing-led localisation, and expand premium products including acrylics, decorative textures, water-based and high-performance coatings.

• 🌍 Focus remains on Tier-2 & Tier-3 expansion, strengthening the dealer network and Sirca Studios, while growing the OEM and institutional business in furniture, modular kitchens and wardrobes.

• 🚚 To enhance supply-chain resilience, Sirca will continue multi-sourcing of key raw materials, maintain higher safety stocks, and use forward cover against currency and freight volatility.

• 🌐 The company also plans to expand exports under the Wembley Valentino brand, with shipments expected to begin gradually in selected international markets over the coming quarters.

• 📈 Management reiterated its focus on protecting market share, building a stronger localized manufacturing base, and delivering sustainable, profitable long-term growth.

SIRCA PAINTS Q1 : OUTLOOK ; Near-term demand stays moderate, but premiumization, renovation demand and organized furniture growth remain intact. 

We expect expect margin recovery as localization and premium mix scale, and target double-digit revenue growth with EBITDA.

The new dedicated Wembley manufacturing facility is fully operational. consolidating multiple production lines into one integrated setup - improving efficiency, quality consistency, supply-chain agility and cost economics

SIRCA PAINTS Q1: OPERATIONAL HIGHLIGHTS 🎨🏡

• 🎯 Acrylic coatings remained the fastest-growing premium wood coatings segment, driven by superior aesthetics, durability, low VOC formulation, and eco-friendly properties.

• 🌟 The company expanded its luxury and super-premium portfolio across Sirca, Oikos, Unico, and Wembley Valentino, while completing localization of acrylic and polyester systems, with commercial production commencing in Q1 FY27. Selected UV systems remain on track.

• 📢 Sirca strengthened brand visibility through partnerships with Architectural Digest and Elle Decor, alongside architect-designer engagement programs and new product launches.

• 🪑 The OEM and institutional business continued to grow, supported by the formalization of India's furniture industry, BIS implementation, and the shift towards organized manufacturing. Margin discipline was maintained through calibrated pricing, sourcing optimization, product mix improvements, and tighter cost controls.

SIRCA PAINTS Q1: STRONG PROFIT GROWTH DESPITE COST PRESSURES 🎨📈

• 📊 Revenue grew 13.8% YoY to ₹130.01 crore, while PAT increased 14.1% YoY to ₹16.21 crore. EPS rose to ₹2.85 from ₹2.59, driven by premium wood coatings, the Wembley portfolio, and deeper pan-India distribution.

• 🌍 Geopolitical tensions, Red Sea freight disruptions, shifting tariff regimes, and EUR-INR volatility kept import and raw material costs elevated during the quarter.

• 🚚 The company managed supply chain disruptions through multi-sourcing, higher safety inventories, and production consolidation at the integrated Wembley facility, ensuring 100% order fulfilment.

• 📉 Industry-wide price corrections and higher channel discounts reduced EBITDA margin to 18.62% (from 19.90%), though absolute EBITDA still grew 6.5% YoY to ₹24.21 crore.

AGI GREENPAC Q1 : Md said Q1 FY27 performance reflected the strength of its core business, supported by an improved product mix, higher operational efficiencies, and sustained demand across alcobev, food & beverage, and specialty glass segments.

• ⚡ Rising energy and raw material costs due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia temporarily weighed on margins during the quarter.

• 💡 The company mitigated the impact through proactive cost optimization and operational efficiency initiatives.

• 🎯 Management expects margin improvement in the coming quarters as input cost volatility eases and the benefits of ongoing efficiency programs continue to accrue.

AGI GREENPAC Q1: STRONG GROWTH BACKED BY CAPACITY EXPANSION 🏭📈

• 📊 Revenue grew 14% YoY to ₹785 crore, while Net Profit increased 12% YoY to ₹99 crore. EBITDA (excluding other income) rose 23% YoY to ₹175 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding to 22%.

• 🏭 The company increased its glass packaging capacity from 1,754 TPD to 2,100 TPD through debottlenecking and is progressing on a 500 TPD Greenfield plant in Madhya Pradesh, expected to be commissioned over the next 7–8 months.

• 🚀 The new plant will take total capacity to 2,600 TPD, representing 48% cumulative capacity growth over the 30 months ending March 2027, strengthening supply capabilities across North India.

• 🥤 AGI Greenpac's aluminium beverage cans project remains on track, with commercial operations targeted by December 2027, enabling packaging synergies across the alcobev and food & beverage segments.

JAIN RESOURCE RECYCLING: RECEIVES APPROVAL TO RESUME MANUFACTURING OPERATIONS 🏭✅

• 🟢 The company has received approval from the Director of Industrial Safety and Health, Chennai to resume manufacturing operations at its Unit-III facility, except for the section affected by the July 14, 2026 fire.

• 🔥 The approval follows a re-inspection confirming that the required safety measures have been implemented and the earlier prohibition order has been lifted for the unaffected manufacturing areas.

• 🏗️ Renovation and restoration work at the fire-affected section is underway, with the company completing the necessary statutory, safety, and regulatory compliances before restarting operations there.

• 📢 The company will continue to provide updates on the progress of restoration work and regulatory approvals for the affected unit.

🟢 Impact: Positive (Resumption of operations at the majority of the facility reduces business disruption and supports a gradual return to normal production.)

SH KELKAR Q1: Revenue grew 14% YoY to ₹662 crore, driven by healthy growth in the Fragrance business and strong performance in the Flavour segment across geographies.

• 📊 Gross margins remained stable, supported by a healthy product mix and proactive raw material planning, while EBITDA margin improved to 13.4% on operating leverage despite higher investments in the expanded global Creative Development Centre (CDC) network.

• 🌸 The Fragrance business delivered healthy growth on sustained customer demand, while Flavour recorded robust international growth through deeper engagement with key customers. Segment margins were impacted by higher R&D and CDC-related operating expenses.

• 🌍 Global Ingredients posted a softer quarter due to weaker demand in select export markets amid geopolitical uncertainty. Management expects FY27 to deliver double-digit revenue growth and improved margins, though quarterly performance may vary with customer ordering patterns and product mix.

SH KELKAR Q1 : SH KELKAR Q1: CFO COMMENTARY 💼📈

• 📊 Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to ₹662 crore, driven by healthy growth in the Fragrance business and strong performance from the Flavour segment across geographies.

• 📈 EBITDA margin improved to 13.4%, supported by operating leverage, while gross margins remained stable due to a healthy product mix and proactive raw material planning.

• 📦 The company has built strategic inventory to ensure supply continuity amid geopolitical uncertainties and raw material volatility, leading to higher working capital. Debt remains in line with earlier guidance.

• 🎯 Management expects double-digit revenue growth and improved margins for FY27, supported by pricing discipline, cost management, better cash conversion, and prudent capital allocation.

SH KELKAR Q1: Management reported a healthy start to FY27, supported by sustained demand across key customer segments and strong business momentum.

• 🤝 The company highlighted its strong customer relationships, diversified product portfolio, and disciplined execution as key drivers of performance.

• 🧪 Continued investments in R&D, Creative Development Centres, and manufacturing capabilities are helping develop differentiated solutions and deepen customer partnerships.

• 🌍 Despite a dynamic operating environment, SH Kelkar believes its diversified presence, expanding capabilities, and established customer base position it well to capitalize on the industry's long-term growth.

ARKADE DEVELOPERS: REPORTS ALLEGED FRAUD BY FORMER CHIEF SALES OFFICER ⚠️

• 🚨 The company has reported alleged misconduct by former Chief Sales Officer Ms. Amita Singh, including diversion of customer transactions, wrongful brokerage payments, alleged forgery of agreements related to additional parking spaces, and misuse of official position.

• 👮 An FIR has been registered at Samata Nagar Police Station, Mumbai, and the company is fully cooperating with the ongoing investigation.

• 💰 The complaint alleges an approximate wrongful financial gain of ₹2 crore, with the final amount subject to investigation by the competent authorities.

🟡 Impact: Neutral (While the incident relates to alleged employee misconduct, the company has taken corrective action and expects no material operational or financial impact.)

Emerald Finance Limited - Q1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call Highlights

Company Overview:
Emerald Finance Limited is a Chandigarh-based technology-driven NBFC focused on Early Wage Access (EWA), retail and MSME lending, and loan origination through its proprietary digital platform. The Company collaborates with over 50 financial institutions, offering a wide range of financial products including personal loans, business loans, gold loans, and EWA solutions.

Financial Performance:

Standalone Q1 FY27 Highlights
* Total Income of ₹6.27 Cr, YoY growth of 32.47%
* EBITDA of ₹5.22 Cr, YoY growth of 35.19%
* Net Profit of ₹3.45 Cr, YoY growth of 31.18%
* EPS of ₹1.00, YoY growth of 31.58%

Consolidated Q1 FY27 Highlights
* Total Income of ₹9.44 Cr, YoY growth of 39.97%
* EBITDA of ₹7.42 Cr, YoY growth of 60.28%
* Net Profit of ₹4.88 Cr, YoY growth of 52.72%
* EPS of ₹1.44, YoY growth of 56.52%

Business Verticals & Operational Performance:

Early Wage Access (EWA)
* EWA portfolio contribution increased from 8% to over 10.5%, with 32 new corporate organizations added during the quarter, taking the active corporate base to 246.
* Monthly EWA run rate reached ₹26 Cr, comprising ₹12.5 Cr of salary advance disbursements and ₹13.5 Cr from cross-selling, with an average ticket size of approximately ₹26,000.

Gold Loan & Lending Business
* Strengthened the lending ecosystem through a strategic partnership with AU Small Finance Bank, while evaluating additional banking partnerships.
* MSME and mortgage portfolios continued to record healthy growth, with MSME loans constituting the majority of the Company's ₹125 Cr AUM (excluding EWA).

Growth & Strategic Initiatives
* Entered into a strategic alliance with Credila Financial Services Limited to offer education loans, generating approximately ₹1 Cr of business in the first month.
* Final testing is underway for Digital Gold & Silver, Micro SIPs, and Pocket Insurance, with commercial launches expected during the current quarter.
* Expanded its corporate footprint beyond North India through new client additions across Chennai, Kolkata, Pune, and Mumbai, while continuing to target larger enterprise clients.

Risk Management & Capital Position
* NPAs remained well under control despite continued portfolio expansion, with a conservative provisioning policy of 0.30%, higher than the regulatory requirement of 0.25%.
* Continued its disciplined underwriting approach by prioritizing asset quality and selectively onboarding corporate clients.
* Net worth stood at approximately ₹90 Cr with borrowings of around ₹27 Cr. The Company also secured an additional ₹10 Cr credit line from ICICI Bank, strengthening its funding profile.

Management Commentary & Outlook:
* Management reiterated its guidance of achieving approximately ₹7 EPS for FY27 and continues to target a 40–50% CAGR over the next two to three years.
* The Company expects product diversification, expanding corporate relationships, and strategic banking partnerships to drive sustainable long-term growth.
* Despite regulatory changes in the gold loan segment, management remains confident in maintaining growth through disciplined execution, prudent risk management, and continued innovation.

Key Takeaways:
* Delivered strong growth across both standalone and consolidated financial performance during Q1 FY27.
* EWA continued to gain traction through strong corporate onboarding, higher portfolio contribution, and increasing cross-selling opportunities.
* Strategic partnerships with Credila Financial Services Limited and AU Small Finance Bank, coupled with upcoming digital financial products, are expected to strengthen Emerald's growth trajectory.
* Strong capitalization, conservative underwriting practices, and a scalable technology-driven business model position the Company for sustained long-term growth.

AUTHUM INVESTMENT: NCLT APPROVES WIND WORLD ACQUISITION PLAN ⚖️🌬️

• ✅ NCLT Ahmedabad has approved the resolution plan submitted by the consortium of Inox Neo Energies Ltd (Lead Member) and Authum Investment & Infrastructure Ltd for the acquisition of Wind World (India) Ltd. 

• 🌬️ Under the approved plan, Inox Neo Energies will acquire Wind World's IPP & power sale business and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) business. 

• 🏢 Authum will acquire identified real estate and other assets of Wind World through the resolution plan. 

• 💰 Authum's financial commitment under the approved resolution plan is approximately ₹350 crore. 

🟢 Impact: Positive (NCLT approval provides certainty to the transaction and enables Authum to acquire strategic assets under the Wind World resolution plan.)

Lloyds Engineering enters into drone manufacturing — and this one's worth reading carefully.

LEWL's subsidiary Lloyds Advance Defence Systems Limited (LADS) has signed a formal agreement with FlyFocus, Poland for licensed manufacturing and joint R&D of UAV products in India.

Three things to note:

1. LEWL now has a dedicated defence subsidiary. The agreement runs through LADS, not the parent — which means the company has quietly set up a separate legal entity specifically for defence. That's a structure play, not just a partnership announcement.

2. This is a step up from the earlier MoU. The Oct-25 tie-up was intent. Today's filing is a licensed manufacturing + joint product development arrangement — actual commercial teeth.

3. Clean deal, no equity or RPT complications. No shares issued, no related-party angle, no promoter connection to FlyFocus. Straightforward arm's length agreement.

The bigger picture — LEWL is clearly positioning LADS as its dedicated defence vehicle, with FlyFocus as the technology anchor for the UAV segment. Watch this entity for further tie-ups as India's defence indigenisation orders start flowing.

~Company’s target is to deliver consistent RoAE of 19.0% - 21.0% and RoAA of 4.2% - 4.7%

APOLLO MICRO SYSTEMS: EMPANELLED BY INDIAN AIR FORCE FOR IPREK PRECISION WEAPON PROGRAMME 🇮🇳🚀

• 🎯 Apollo Micro Systems has been empanelled by the Indian Air Force as a Prime Development Agency for the Indigenous Precision Range Extension Kit (IPREK) under the Make-II (Industry Funded) defence programme. 

• 💣 IPREK converts existing 500 kg unguided bombs into long-range precision glide weapons with 3-metre accuracy and 80–100 km standoff range, improving strike capability while reducing import dependence. 

• 🛰️ The system integrates NavIC satellite navigation, Electro-Optical (EO), Infrared (IIR) and DSMAC guidance for high-precision operations, including GPS-denied environments. 

• 📦 Initial procurement is expected to cover 500+ IPREK units, creating a multi-year revenue opportunity for Apollo Micro Systems if the programme progresses successfully. 

• 🌍 The company estimates a ₹20,000+ crore domestic import-substitution opportunity over the next decade and sees IPREK as a gateway to future precision weapon programmes for the Army, Navy and defence exports. 

⚠️ Note: This is an empanelment, not a firm commercial order. Revenue will accrue only after a formal Project Sanction Order (PSO) and subsequent procurement contract. 

🟢 Impact: Positive (A strategic entry into India's high-value precision-guided munitions segment with significant long-term opportunity, though near-term revenues depend on future orders.)

• Management is aiming for a full-year EBITDA per kg of INR 44-45, exceeding the initial target of INR 42-43, driven by consolidation benefits and improved efficiencies.

• Food and FMCG are expected to grow at an 18-20% CAGR, while Pharma is projected for a 40-50% CAGR over the next three to four years, with a Pharma revenue target of INR 50-55 crores for the current year.

• Overall volume growth for the full year is targeted at 10-12%, with 10% still considered achievable, and Paint volumes are expected to grow in the 10-15% range.

• CapEx for FY27 is projected at INR 90 crores, including INR 25-30 crores for Pharma, and the company plans for 10-12% annual capacity additions.

Ganesh Housing: Guidance - - Concall Update

• For FY '27, revenue is projected to be INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores, with PAT ranging from INR300 crores to INR325 crores.

• PAT growth for FY '27 is expected to be maintained or rise by only about 10% due to a one-time tax burden in Q1 FY '27 from the One91 Thaltej land sale.

• Lease rentals from Million Minds will commence in Q4 FY '27, with full-year rentals expected in FY '28, potentially exceeding INR75 crores.

• The company prefers to provide guidance year-on-year rather than for multiple years due to market changes.

• Plans for the Godhavi land parcel include a mix of development, plotted development, construction, and land sales, with exact details to be announced later in the year.

Associated Alcohols & Breweries: Guidance - - Concall Update

• For FY '27, management is confident in delivering around 30% volume growth in the IMFL Proprietary portfolio, while also expecting its revenue to grow at the same rate year-on-year.

• The SDF distillery in Kerala is expected to become operational by December '26, with full-fledged operations planned from April onwards, aiming for a capacity of 3.5 to 4 lakh cases per month.

• Management targets specific market shares for new product launches: 3% to 4% for RTD, 4% for Malt over time, and 10% to 15% for Tequila within its targeted 40,000-case market segment.

• For the ethanol business, management expects quota allocation to improve in coming months and anticipates a gradual performance improvement as prices likely bottomed out, with better realization from the October tender onwards.

• The IMFL licensed business is projected to achieve approximately 1 million cases annually.

Nitin Gadkari moves Bombay High Court over alleged misinformation on E20 ethanol policy

Union Minister Nitin Gadkari has approached the Bombay High Court against social media posts that allegedly link him and his family to business gains from India’s E20 ethanol blending programme.

According to the civil suit, the disputed content includes posts, deepfake images, and videos claiming that Gadkari and his family benefited financially from the ethanol blending initiative.

The petition argues that these allegations are false and notes that the E20 ethanol blending policy is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, not by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways headed by Gadkari.

The Bombay High Court has permitted Gadkari to proceed with a civil suit against Meta, other social media platforms, and unidentified individuals or entities allegedly responsible for creating and disseminating the defamatory content. The case seeks legal remedies against the spread of what Gadkari describes as misinformation targeting him and his family.

text:
India Built a Phone Export Industry. Now It Needs Customers It Doesn't Have.

India's handset export scheme is aimed at a global market where roughly 61% of units sit outside Apple and Samsung and are served by Chinese brands using Chinese assemblers. The binding constraint is therefore anchor customer access, not incentive quantum or installed capacity, which is why the same policy tool that worked domestically may not repeat offshore. 

This is falsified if a non Apple Indian assembler announces a multi year export contract with a top ten global brand.
